items.detail: Real CLI run from scratch dir /tmp/ralphscratch2 (no .speclang/): `tsx src/ralph-loop.ts /tmp/ralphscratch2/state.db` printed 'Applying migration 1..8' then 'Ralph Loop state database ready at /tmp/ralphscratch2/state.db (schema version 8)' and kept running (killed by timeout, EXIT:124 — not exit 1). Read-only DB inspection showed tables tasks/steering_packets/specs, tasks columns id,title,description,status,assigned_to,created_at,updated_at, steering_packets.payload and specs.layer present. Default-path run from /tmp/ralphscratch created .speclang/speclang.db (94KB) and exited 1 with RalphLoopStateInitError naming the file and the `rm -f .speclang/speclang.db` recovery step — no bare SqliteError. Reachability: src/ralph-loop.ts:452-472 main() -> LoopController.create() -> ensureStateDirectory + openStateDatabase + withStateDatabase(bootstrapRalphLoopState) at src/ralph-loop.ts:236-247, which runs migrate() (src/db/migrations.ts:672) plus RALPH_LOOP_SCHEMA_SQL and the additive payload/layer columns. Tests: `npx vitest run tests/db/ralph-loop-fresh-state.test.ts` -> 'Test Files 1 passed (1)', 'Tests 7 passed (7)', exit 0; the entry-point case at tests/db/ralph-loop-fresh-state.test.ts:290-330 spawns the real tsx entry in a fresh project dir and asserts stderr has no /SqliteError|no such table|directory does not exist/, exitCode !== 1, stillRunning true, and tasks/specs tables exist. Broader runs: `npx vitest run tests/db/` -> 5 files / 32 tests passed; full suite `npx vitest run --passWithNoTests` -> 'Test Files 112 passed | 4 skipped (116)', 'Tests 1944 passed | 58 skipped (2002)', zero FAIL lines. [resolution 0.17; src/ralph-loop.ts]

findings.detection: new exported symbol `bootstrapRalphLoopState` is called only from within the same file's `create()`; the test imports `LoopController`, `RALPH_LOOP_SCHEMA_SQL`, `RALPH_LOOP_INIT_FAILED_CODE`, `RalphLoopStateInitError` but never `bootstrapRalphLoopState`
findings.detail: The function is exported but no other module or test references it, so the export is dead surface area (minor wiring smell, not a break).

findings.detection: `withStateDatabase(db, dbPath, () => bootstrapRalphLoopState(db, dbPath))` wraps a synchronous callback whose return value is discarded; if `withStateDatabase` is async or returns a promise, the bootstrap runs outside the try/catch's awaited scope
findings.detail: The call site does not `await` the result of `withStateDatabase`, so any rejection from an async wrapper would escape the surrounding try/catch and bypass the `RalphLoopStateInitError` conversion the diff claims to guarantee.

findings.detection: failure-path test for `RalphLoopStateInitError` only covers the `mkdirSync` failure (parent is a file); no test exercises the `migrate`/`db.exec` failure path or the `STATE_DB_CORRUPT_CODE` re-throw branch in `create()`
findings.detail: The `catch` block has two branches — re-throw on `STATE_DB_CORRUPT_CODE` and wrap otherwise — and only the wrap branch is tested; the corrupt-DB passthrough is asserted nowhere in this file.

findings.detection: `addColumnIfMissing` interpolates `table`/`column`/`declaration` into SQL via template literals, whereas the surrounding code (e.g. `openStateDatabase`, migrations) uses prepared statements or fixed SQL constants
findings.detail: The comment justifies the interpolation as internal literals, but the helper accepts arbitrary strings and would silently produce invalid SQL if a caller ever passed a non-literal; a fixed-SQL constant per column would match the file's existing style.

findings.detection: `console.error` is used for the success/readiness line inside `bootstrapRalphLoopState`, while the rest of the module reports via thrown errors and `main()`'s `console.error` on failure only
findings.detail: Emitting a normal-path informational message on stderr diverges from the module's convention of reserving stderr for failures, and the test relies on that stderr string as its readiness signal.

review.summary: The bootstrap wiring is functionally coherent, but the `withStateDatabase` call is not awaited (risking an uncaught rejection that bypasses the new error wrapper), the corrupt-DB re-throw branch has no test, and a few convention drifts (dead export, interpolated DDL, stderr for success) are present.
